analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities closed higher Wednesday (S&P +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%, Dow +0.49%), ending a bit off best levels. The equal-weight S&P trailed the cap-weighted index by about 50 bp.

The AI trade led the market, with neoclouds the standouts. SOX posted its third strong gain in four sessions and is up about 17% from last Thursday's sharp drop. NVDA stabilized while MSFT, AMZN and META were weaker.

The rally followed CoreWeave's beat-and-raise, positive headlines on Anthropic's coming IPO, a strong acceleration in OpenAI's Q3 revenue growth and positioning support. The dollar index rose 0.7%, gold fell 0.7%, silver gained 1.5% and WTI settled up 0.6%.

The US bond market was closed for Veterans Day after a big backup in Treasury yields on Tuesday, which followed hotter-than-expected CPI and hawkish Fed comments. There was no data or Fedspeak Wednesday.

Thursday brings jobless claims, a $25B 30-year bond auction and several Fed speakers. Friday's PPI has taken outsized importance: headline expected +0.4% m/m after +1.3% in September, core +0.3% after +0.7%.

CoreWeave: $132.5B backlog, about $9B in prepayments and deposits from signed contracts in the next three months, no parent-level unsecured debt through 2027, parent-level capital needs below $5B through 2027. About 300K GPUs roll off in 2027-28, with renewals potentially generating nearly $10B with no additional capex.

Anthropic's bankers reportedly target a $1.5T IPO valuation, up from $1.4T the day before, with orders multiple times the shares available (FT, Bloomberg). A higher price would lift the raise to over $100B. JonesTrading is marketing a block of up to $500M at a 3-5% premium to the final IPO price.

OpenAI reported $10B quarterly revenue for the period ending September, up 50% from the prior quarter, with ARR at $50B. It is seeking funding at a $1.25T valuation, down from the $1.5T investors initially sought (Reuters).

Treasury yields posted their steepest daily rise since April 2025 on Tuesday. Waller mentioned a possible 50 bp move, Logan said quicker hikes may be needed, Goolsbee called the CPI report disturbing and Bowman said there is still work to do. Markets price about an 85% chance of a December Fed hike and more likelihood of three further hikes in 2027, versus two before CPI.

The Trump administration is adopting an economic-pressure strategy on Iran, including a naval blockade operation named Iron Gate (Axios). Rubio said major combat operations are no longer needed and a diplomatic deal is unlikely soon. Iran's security chief said Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets seven preconditions. Al Arabiya reported a preliminary deal allowing down-blending of enriched uranium to 3.67%, IAEA inspections and release of $6-9B of frozen assets.

European equities closed higher Wednesday (Germany +1.2%, France +0.7%, UK +0.8%), with cyclicals leading. Tech and chip stocks gained on AI infrastructure enthusiasm. The OAT-Bund spread narrowed about 1.3bp to 146.8bp.

ECB's Lane backs a December hike if data does not shift and sees inflation a little above 4% by year-end. October eurozone PMI eased to a four-month low of 51.7 and S&P Global sees quarterly growth of about 0.3%. Bundesbank's Nagel signaled an upward revision to German growth forecasts next month.

NIESR sees peak UK inflation of 4.4% in February (BoE forecast 4.9%) and a case for higher rates. Markets price Bank Rate at 4.75% next year, and NIESR says about that level is needed. Sell-side expects another BoE hike in February, though Lombardelli said December is live.

Dutch TTF gas rose a second session after falling from a near-€104/MWh early-November peak to about €79/MWh Monday. Europe's energy import bill is up over €127B since the Iran conflict began. Sell-side sees winter gas at €70-90/MWh.

Merz threatened to veto the EU 2028-2034 budget over Ukraine funding linkage. The EU has promised to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's €70B gap, about €45B, most likely through new joint debt. A special summit is set for the end of the month.
Asia was mixed Wednesday: Japan +1.31%, Hong Kong -1.06%, China -0.46%, with the Hang Seng at the bottom of its trading range. JGB and regional yields jumped from recent lows.

BOJ is considering a third hike this year, the first such pace since 1989. OIS pricing for a December hike fell to 52% last Friday from 79% after the Nikkei's third-largest absolute drop on record, then recovered to 76% Tuesday. The October Summary of Opinions was mostly hawkish.

China is weighing a possible 25% tax on government bond interest income. One estimate implies a 52 bp rise in the 10Y CGB yield to keep the same after-tax return. China 10Y trades near a record low, and banks are raising dollar deposit rates to curb yuan strength, with the yuan near its highest since May 2022.

SoftBank reported a Q2 net loss of JPY1.115T ($7.1B), with an H1 impairment of about JPY600B tied to US AI data center procurement costs. NAV fell JPY12.5T to JPY59.9T in September versus June, and LTV rose 2.9 ppt to 15.9%. The CFO said the latest OpenAI funding round could produce significant Q3 gains.
TSMC will invest $500M each in Anthropic and OpenAI. Alibaba's chip design unit T-Head filed for a Hong Kong IPO.

Notable US earnings moves: CoreWeave +24.7%, Riskified +22.3%, Rumble +16.6%, Mercury Systems +5.7% on beats and raises. Applied Aerospace & Defense -13.3% on a guidance cut, Suja Life -12.9% (Goldman downgrade to neutral), Grocery Outlet -6.4% on a lower EBITDA guide. Costco announced a $30/sh special dividend and $4B buyback.

Notable European moves: Siemens Energy +10.7% (Q4 EPS €1.49 vs €1.39 est, buyback expanded to up to €9B through FY30), CSG -20.3% (Q3 revenue €1.51B vs €1.81B est, FY EBIT margin guide cut to ~21%), Voestalpine -5.9%, Alcon -4.4% on below-consensus narrowed guidance, Vestas -3.8%.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 beat and raise with a $132.5B backlog and no parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 eased funding concerns. Stock rose 24.7%.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3: beat and raise, $132.5B backlog, stock +24.7%.
Riskified Q3: earnings and revenue beat, FY guidance raised, stock +22.3%.
Rumble Q3: adjusted EBITDA and revenue beat, Q4 revenue guide brackets consensus, stock +16.6%.
Mercury Systems FQ1: EPS, revenue and EBITDA sharply beat, EBITDA margin up about 650bps y/y, FY27 outlook raised, stock +5.7%.
Grocery Outlet Q3: EPS in line, revenue beat, EBITDA missed, FY26 comp outlook raised but EBITDA guidance lowered, stock -6.4%.
Siemens Energy Q4: EPS €1.49 vs consensus est €1.39, FY27 margin guide 14-16% vs est 14.2%, stock +10.7%.
Alcon Q3: core EPS $0.91 reported vs consensus est $0.88, revenue $2.72B vs est $2.73B, FY guidance narrowed below consensus, stock -4.4%.
CSG Q3: revenue €1.51B vs consensus est €1.81B, FY operating EBIT margin guidance cut to ~21% from 24-25%, stock -20.3%.
Vestas Q3: net income €323M vs consensus est €380M, revenue €5.68B vs est €6.00B, stock -3.8%.
SoftBank Q2: net loss JPY1.115T, stock -0.4%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Drove the steepest one-day Treasury yield rise since April 2025 and lifted December Fed hike pricing to about 85%.
Expected Friday after +1.3% in September. A hot print would reinforce Fed hike pricing.
Four-month low, but growth is resilient enough that hawks see room for another ECB hike.
Below the BoE's 4.9% forecast but NIESR sees persistence risk and a case for higher rates.
Market-implied, with three more hikes more likely in 2027.
Government forecast, with 2027 growth forecast at about 1%.

risk_factors: Hot PPI Friday could extend the Treasury selloff and raise Fed hike odds further.
AI funding concerns persist despite CoreWeave's reassurance, and SoftBank is booking AI data center impairments.
US data center regulation uncertainty could keep equity volatility elevated.
The Iran conflict and European gas supply into winter, with low stockpiles and imports lagging.
Central banks tightening into a slowdown (ECB, BoE, BOJ, Fed).
China bond income tax could lift yields and unsettle fixed income markets.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index at 17.49, down 10.12% on the day and down 31.79% week to date.
SOX is up about 17% from last Thursday's sharp drop, with positioning cited as support for the rally.
The Nikkei had its third-largest absolute drop on record last Friday.
geopolitical: US adopting indefinite economic pressure on Iran including naval blockade operation Iron Gate, with renewed strikes called unlikely.

Iran's security chief says Hormuz would reopen within two days if seven preconditions are met. Al Arabiya reports a preliminary deal on uranium down-blending, IAEA access and release of $6-9B of frozen assets.
Merz threatens to veto the EU 2028-2034 budget over linkage to Ukraine funding. Slovakia, Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria want to opt out of any Ukraine loan.
Zelensky says Europe must act fast on who represents it in peace talks with Russia.
US data center regulations may follow the Democratic midterm victory, but are not expected to be clear until at least next summer (NLI Research).
cross_bank_references: Goldman Sachs downgraded Suja Life to neutral from buy.
New Street Research downgraded Infrastrutture Wireless Italiane to neutral from buy on 10 November.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot CPI and hawkish Fed speakers (Waller on a possible 50 bp move, Logan on quicker hikes) push December hike pricing to about 85%, with three more hikes in 2027 now more likely.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI-led equity rally and positioning support continue despite higher yields, and Friday's PPI is expected to cool to +0.4% headline and +0.3% core from +1.3% and +0.7%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A PPI print below the +0.4% headline and +0.3% core expectations on Friday would soften hike pricing.
